extracted.intended_audience: press officers, science journalists, and media outlets reporting on research
extracted.subtask_description: A short public notice issued to media and the public announcing that previously press‑released research has been formally retracted, providing the reasons, bibliographic details, and instructions for reporters. It is intended to correct the record and direct recipients to stop citing the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement that the research has been retracted
rubrics_metrics.description: “The research ... has been retracted.” (page opens with the heading and the sentence: 'The research “Acupuncture for low back and/or pelvic pain during pregnancy: ...” ... has been retracted.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with an unequivocal statement that the work is retracted so readers immediately understand the status change (e.g., heading 'Retraction notice of previously press released research' plus explicit sentence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the original research (title, journal, year)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice names the article title and where/when it was published: 'The research “Acupuncture for low back and/or pelvic pain during pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials,” published in the open access journal BMJ Open in 2022, has been retracted.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full identifying information for the affected paper (full title, journal name, and publication year) so recipients can unambiguously locate the work being retracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: State that the work was previously press released (context for media)
rubrics_metrics.description: “This research was press released in November 2022 under the title of ‘Acupuncture can relieve lower back/pelvic pain often experienced during pregnancy.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the research had an earlier press release, explicitly note that to help media trace prior coverage and correct past reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise summary of the reasons for retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: “Following publication of the research, various issues concerning its design and reporting methods came to light, none of which was amenable to correction, prompting the decision to retract.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise the nature of the problems (design/reporting flaws). Be specific where possible about the types of flaws without publishing exhaustive investigation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific examples of fundamental flaws where available
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice lists examples: 'There were fundamental flaws with the research, including the control group selection and data extraction, not amenable to correction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, cite concrete issues (e.g., control group selection, data extraction errors) so readers understand the basis for the retraction and why correction was not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the investigation and decision-making process
rubrics_metrics.description: “The editors and integrity team investigated the issues with the authors.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate who investigated (editors/integrity team) and that authors were involved in the inquiry to show due process leading to the retraction decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide retraction notice bibliographic details (DOI and publication time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page gives the retraction DOI and scheduled publication timing: 'doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2021-056878ret' and 'will be published at 23.30 hours UK (BST) time Tuesday 11 June 2024.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the DOI (or link) for the formal retraction notice and, if relevant, when/where the retraction text will be or was published so reporters can cite the authoritative source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct instruction to media to stop citing the retracted work
rubrics_metrics.description: “Please ensure that you no longer cite this research in any future reporting.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly tell news outlets and other users to cease citing or relying on the retracted work and to correct previous coverage where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal attribution (where the retraction is recorded)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice states the journal: 'Journal BMJ Open.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the journal that issued/hosts the retraction so readers know the archival source and can consult the journal record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/provider disclaimer about responsibility for posted releases
rubrics_metrics.description: “AAAS and EurekAlert! are not responsible for the accuracy of news releases posted to EurekAlert! by contributing institutions or for the use of any information through the EurekAlert system.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include or preserve platform disclaimers clarifying that the distributing service is not responsible for contributors' content and for users' use of information.
